blogPosts.title: How Much Does Solar Panel Installation Cost in Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Find out the real cost of solar panels in Melbourne for 2026, including rebates, system sizes and payback periods specific to Southbank homes.
body: Thinking about solar panels for your Southbank home? The cost of solar installation in Melbourne has dropped significantly over the past few years, but 2026 brings new rebate structures and system options. A typical 6.6kW system now ranges from $5,000 to $8,500 after the federal STC discount, with smaller systems starting around $3,500. But the final price depends on your roof type, orientation and any additional work like switchboard upgrades.

For Southbank homeowners, many apartments and townhouses have shared roofs or limited space, so we often recommend smaller high-efficiency panels or balcony systems. Our team at All Electric Homes specialises in custom solar designs for compact urban spaces. We also help you access the Solar Victoria rebate, which can knock another $1,400 off a solar battery system if paired with solar.

The payback period for a solar-only system in Melbourne is typically 3 to 5 years, thanks to our high feed-in tariffs and strong sunlight even in winter. With a battery, payback stretches to 7–10 years, but the energy independence is worth it for many families. We always run a personalised savings calculator during your free consultation so you know exactly what to expect.

One major factor often overlooked is the condition of your existing electrical panel. Older homes in Southbank may need a switchboard upgrade to handle solar safely. That adds $800–$1,500 to the total cost, but it's essential for safety and compliance. All Electric Homes includes a full electrical safety check with every solar quote.

Another cost consideration is the inverter. A standard string inverter costs $1,000–$2,000, while microinverters (better for shaded roofs) can cost double. We recommend microinverters for Southbank apartments with partial shading from nearby buildings. They also allow individual panel monitoring, so you can track performance down to the module.

Installation time is usually one to two days for a standard house, but apartments may require extra coordination with the body corporate. All Electric Homes handles all council and owner corporation approvals as part of our service. We also offer interest-free payment plans through Brighte and other lenders, making solar more accessible.

Don't forget ongoing maintenance. Solar panels need occasional cleaning – Melbourne's dusty summers and bird droppings can reduce output by 10–15%. We recommend a professional clean every two years for around $200. Most panels come with a 25-year performance warranty, so your investment is protected.

To get an accurate quote for your Southbank home, book a free on-site assessment with All Electric Homes. We'll measure your roof, analyse your energy bills, and recommend the best system for your budget. Start saving on electricity from day one.

blogPosts.title: Heat Pump Hot Water vs Gas: Which is Cheaper in Melbourne?
blogPosts.excerpt: Compare the running costs of heat pump hot water systems versus gas for Melbourne homes in 2026. We break down rebates, installation and long-term savings.
body: If you're still using a gas hot water system in your Southbank home, you're likely paying more than you need to. Heat pump hot water systems use up to 75% less energy than standard electric systems and are cheaper to run than gas in most Melbourne homes. But the upfront cost is higher – expect $2,500 to $4,500 installed, compared to $1,200 for a new gas unit.

The good news: the Victorian Government offers a rebate of up to $1,000 for heat pump hot water under the Solar Victoria program, plus an additional $300 for replacing gas. That slashes the upfront price. And once you have solar panels, you can run your heat pump mostly on free solar energy, bringing running costs close to zero.

Gas hot water systems may seem cheaper upfront, but gas connection fees add $300–$400 per year to your bill even if you use no gas. Plus, gas prices are expected to rise as supply tightens. In Melbourne, a typical household spends $600–$900 per year on gas hot water. A heat pump on off-peak electricity costs around $200–$350, or less with solar.

Installation is straightforward for most homes, but older Southbank apartments may have limited space. Heat pumps are compact – many fit on a balcony or wall bracket. Our plumbers handle all plumbing connections and can also abolish your old gas meter if you're going all-electric. That removes the gas supply charge permanently.

One concern we hear is that heat pumps don't work well in Melbourne's cold winters. Actually, modern units are designed for temperatures down to -10°C. They pull heat from the air even on frosty mornings. Some models include a backup electric booster for very cold days, but that's rarely needed in Southbank's climate.

Noise is another consideration. Heat pumps produce a low hum – about 50 decibels from 3 metres. That's quieter than a gas unit's burner. Place it away from bedroom windows and you won't notice it. We also recommend models with a 'silent mode' for overnight operation.

Maintenance is minimal: just check the air filter every six months and clean the outdoor coils annually. Most units have a 5- to 7-year warranty. Our team at All Electric Homes includes the first year of maintenance free with every heat pump installation.

Switching to heat pump hot water is one of the smartest energy upgrades a Melbourne homeowner can make. Combine it with solar and you're on track for a true zero-energy home. Contact All Electric Homes for a free quote tailored to your Southbank property.

blogPosts.title: EV Charger Installation Guide for Southbank Apartment Owners
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything Southbank apartment owners need to know about installing an EV charger – strata approval, power upgrades, rebates and smart charging tips.
body: Owning an electric vehicle in a Southbank apartment comes with unique challenges. Most apartment car parks don't have dedicated charging infrastructure, but with the right planning, you can install a personal EV charger. All Electric Homes specialises in apartment EV installations and works with body corporates to get approval quickly.

The first step is checking your car park's power supply. Many apartment buildings have single-phase electricity shared across parking spots. Our electricians assess the available capacity and may recommend a load management system that shares power between chargers without tripping the main switch. This is essential for older Southbank buildings.

Strata approval is often the biggest hurdle. You'll need to submit an application to the owners' corporation, including a detailed plan from a licensed electrician. All Electric Homes provides a complete strata pack with diagrams, compliance certificates and insurance documents. We've helped over 50 apartment owners get approval in Melbourne's Bayside area.

The type of charger matters too. We recommend a 7kW smart charger with Wi-Fi connectivity. These chargers let you schedule charging during off-peak hours (e.g., midnight to 6am) when electricity is cheapest. Some models even integrate with solar panels to charge from excess solar power only.

Costs for apartment EV charger installation range from $1,500 to $3,500, depending on distance from your meter, need for a sub-board, and whether you want a pedestal or wall-mounted unit. The Victorian Government's EV Charger Rebate can cover up to $1,000 of the cost for eligible installations.

Safety is paramount in shared car parks. Our installations include earth leakage protection, cable management to prevent tripping, and weatherproof enclosures. We also install lockable chargers to prevent unauthorised use. Every setup is fully compliant with Australian standards.

Future-proofing is wise: install a charger with at least 7kW capacity and a Type 2 socket (the standard in Australia). If you later upgrade to a faster onboard charger, you won't need new wiring. We also recommend installing a separate meter to simplify reimbursement from your body corporate.

Ready to charge your EV at home? All Electric Homes handles everything from strata submissions to final testing. Book a free consultation today and we'll design a tailored EV charging solution for your Southbank apartment.

blogPosts.title: Induction Cooktop vs Gas: Why Southbank Homeowners Are Switching
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover why induction cooktops are replacing gas in Southbank kitchens – faster cooking, lower energy bills, better indoor air quality and government rebates.
body: Walk into any new Southbank apartment development and you'll likely see an induction cooktop. Induction is rapidly becoming the preferred choice for Melbourne homeowners who want a modern, efficient kitchen. But if you're used to gas, you might wonder: is it really better? The short answer is yes – for performance, health and cost.

Induction uses electromagnetic energy to heat the pan directly, not the cooktop surface. That means water boils in half the time of gas, and your kitchen stays cooler in summer. Temperature control is instant and precise – you can simmer a sauce or sear a steak with zero lag. Professional chefs are increasingly choosing induction for its responsiveness.

Indoor air quality is a huge benefit. Gas cooktops produce nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide and other pollutants that can worsen asthma and respiratory issues, especially in small apartments with poor ventilation. Induction produces zero combustion byproducts, so your indoor air stays clean. Victoria's ban on gas connections in new homes from 2024 is accelerating this shift.

Running costs: induction is about three times more efficient than gas. A typical Southbank household spends $150–$250 per year on gas cooking; induction on electricity costs around $60–$120, especially if you have solar panels. Over a decade, that's a significant saving.

Installation involves running a dedicated 32A circuit from your switchboard. If you already have electric cooking, it's often a simple swap. For homes with gas, our electricians will install the circuit, and our plumbers will cap the gas line safely. All Electric Homes also handles gas meter abolition if you're going fully electric.

You will need induction-compatible cookware – magnetic stainless steel, cast iron or enamel. Most modern pans work fine. If you're worried about the cost of new pots, check your current set with a magnet; many stainless steel pans are already induction-ready. We provide a free magnet tester with every installation.

Safety features are second to none: induction cooktops won't turn on unless a pan is present, and they automatically shut off if no pan is detected. The surface stays cool to the touch, making it much safer if you have young children or elderly family members.

Ready to upgrade your Southbank kitchen? All Electric Homes offers a complete induction cooktop installation service, including electrical work, gas disconnection and rebate application. Contact us for a free quote and take the first step toward a healthier, cheaper, more efficient home.
